text: You ordered a tiny item online, like a phone charger. You expect a neat, compact package, perfectly sized for it. You just want your small item delivered efficiently.
But then a delivery truck arrives, handing you a colossal cardboard box. It's comically oversized for the tiny item rattling inside. Your expectation is shattered.
You stare at the empty space, full of packing peanuts. "Why all this waste? Are they just bad packers? Or trying to protect it with excessive padding?"
The truth: it’s not about your item, but the system. Warehouses use only a few standardized box sizes, optimized for shipping containers and speed.
This standardization makes the entire logistics chain incredibly efficient, saving companies vast time and money. The cost? Visible cardboard and air, hiding optimized machinery.
So next time your tiny trinket arrives in a giant box, you’ll still feel absurd. But now, you’ll see the silent, streamlined logic.
